scope: Static in-repo caller/contract trace of every TurboVec integration point (HTTP, gRPC, two independent N-API loading paths, spawned CLI). No runtime routing, config default, or code was changed. Live health probes reused from the existing parent-atlas-transport-owner-matrix-v1.json census, not re-probed this pass.
keyDistinction: logical search owner != transport protocol != executor binding. This report's central finding is that HTTP and gRPC are NOT two competing owners of the same capability -- they cover two DIFFERENT TurboVec operations (ANN /search vs candidate /rerank), each with its own separately-config-gated primary path. Both operations independently degrade to real Qdrant when their TurboVec transport is unavailable.

http.realOperationCalled: POST /rerank only -- confirmed by grepping every fetch() call in turbovec-search.ts (2 total: 1 to Qdrant directly, 1 to `${sidecarUrl}/rerank`). No code path in this file issues an HTTP request to a /search-shaped endpoint.

callers.note: This function's OWN candidate generation is real Qdrant (searchQdrantWithVectors) plus local SOM-cluster pruning, not a TurboVec ANN call. TurboVec HTTP only reranks candidates Qdrant already found. Calling this the 'TurboVec HTTP search path' (as prior census entries did) is imprecise -- it is a TurboVec-assisted Qdrant rerank path.

logicalOwner.secondaryCapability: TurboVec /rerank (a genuinely different operation, not a competing owner of /search) is reachable via qdrant-search.ts's TurboVecSearchBackend, but config-gated off by default (CODEBASE_ANN_BACKEND=qdrant).
ownerCandidates: HTTP (live fallback for /search inside the same function; separately, live primary for /rerank when explicitly enabled)

The two direct-gRPC callers (context-assembler.ts, atlas/search route) bypass the shared fallback wrapper -- not a vote-duplication risk, but a real fallback-behavior inconsistency across callers, flagged above.

voteInvariant.evidence: Traced every real caller of every TurboVec transport (HTTP, gRPC, both N-API adapters, CLI) against rrf-integration.ts's actual 3-lane Promise.allSettled fusion call. Exactly one TurboVec-derived lane (turbovecPromise, via turbovec-prefilter.ts) reaches RRF. The Qdrant lane in the same fusion (qdrantPromise) calls a separate function (queryQdrantVectorSignal) with no TurboVec involvement. qdrant-search.ts's TurboVecSearchBackend and both N-API adapters are either config-gated off by default or non-RRF diagnostic/dead paths -- none contribute a second vote today.

parityProbe.reason: HTTP and gRPC do not expose equivalent operations to compare -- gRPC's live caller uses ANN /search; HTTP's live caller uses candidate /rerank on Qdrant-sourced input. A parity probe between them would compare two different capabilities, not two transports of the same one, and would produce a misleading result. The genuinely comparable pair (gRPC /search vs HTTP /search, both reachable inside turbovec-prefilter.ts::turbovecSearch()) was not probed this pass -- flagged as the correct future parity-probe target if one is wanted, distinct from the naive HTTP-vs-gRPC framing this gate started from.

resultRationale: For the capability that actually matters for retrieval fusion (ANN /search contributing to RRF), single ownership is objectively established by existing code: turbovec-prefilter.ts::turbovecSearch() is the one call site, gRPC-primary/HTTP-fallback within one function, wired into exactly one RRF lane, with the alternate TurboVec-touching paths (HTTP-only rerank backend, both N-API adapters, CLI wrapper) either config-gated off by default, architected as non-voting diagnostics, or dead code. No operator decision is required to establish this specific invariant. An operator decision (not made here) would still be needed to decide whether to (a) reconcile the two independent N-API loader implementations, (b) unify the two direct-gRPC callers onto the shared fallback-safe wrapper, or (c) remove the dead-duplicate searchCodebaseAnn definition -- all flagged, none acted on.
